circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be constructed, following Bahrain and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street course encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with various supporting motorsport events. The venue maintains an FIA Grade 1 classification for international racing standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, the track was renamed and returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 through 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital built along Baku Boulevard, measuring 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as Formula One's fourth-longest venue. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual F1 race alongside various motorsport categories including GP2 and endurance racing. The track, which holds FIA Grade 1 status and features multiple configuration options, previously accommodated touring car racing from 2006 until 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 km and features a balanced mix of extended straights and varied corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7. 004 km circuit in Wallonia, Belgium, has been a staple of international motorsport since hosting its inaugural Grand Prix in 1925. It served as a venue for the first Formula One season in 1950 and currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix annually, with only brief interruptions in 2003 and 2006 breaking its otherwise continuous presence on the championship calendar since 1985.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in international single-seater racing, the venue has also accommodated various other motorsport series including prototype sports cars, open-wheel championships, and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading district, is a motorsport venue renowned for staging the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. In addition to hosting the Formula One championship race, the track began welcoming the Shanghai ePrix from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone and Whittlebury in Northamptonshire, this English racing venue has been hosting the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with Aintree and Brands Hatch between 1955 and 1986, the championship event became a permanent fixture at the circuit from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit located near Budapest, Hungary, that hosts the annual Formula One Hungarian Grand Prix and made history in 1986 as the first F1 race held in the Eastern Bloc. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. It has hosted the Italian Grand Prix almost continuously since 1949, making it one of the few tracks present throughout Formula One's history, and earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its distinctively fast layout featuring lengthy straights and high-speed bends.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and is operated by a Honda subsidiary. The 155,000-capacity facility is renowned as a premier venue for Formula One racing and other major international motorsport competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares. The layout weaves past iconic casino resorts and landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment centered on the entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro, both of whom died in racing accidents in the 1960s and 1970s. The circuit has been the venue for the Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, most recently hosting the event continuously since 2015 on its current configuration, with the race now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix from 2021 onwards.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners designed specifically for Formula One racing. Built by Apex Circuit Design, the track hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the championship calendar in 2022 and generates average qualifying speeds near 139 mph.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street course that winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling Monaco's harbour. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely called "Monte Carlo" as the majority of the track runs through the Monte Carlo district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track featuring distinctive banked corners and dramatic elevation changes that wind through the sandy terrain. The venue hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026, earning its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname from fans due to its unique combination of steep banking at corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz alongside rapid height variations.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km racing venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, serving as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix beginning in 2021 and recently welcoming Formula E racing from 2025 onward.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, utilizing public roads around the Marina Bay waterfront for its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Montmeló's Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP and the FIA World Endurance Championship, while previously accommodating various other racing series ranging from IndyCar to rally competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British driver who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently racing for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso, a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin, is a two-time Formula One world champion, claiming his titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond Formula One, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both the premier single-seater and world endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British driver Oliver Bearman currently races in Formula One, competing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabriel Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently drives for Audi in the Formula One championship series.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He has secured two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while previously competing for Mercedes, along with accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine. He represents his nation in the sport's premier racing category.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver currently racing for Alpine in Formula One, previously claimed his sole career victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix when competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved a record-tying seven World Championship titles matching Michael Schumacher's total. He holds numerous circuit records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-season career. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver competing in endurance racing with BMW through WRT and part-time in NASCAR, previously participated in Formula One across two separate periods spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver currently competing for McLaren, where he secured the world championship in 2025. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Haas. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that includes six race victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull, establishing himself among the sport's most accomplished competitors.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver currently racing for McLaren, has secured nine Formula One victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons from 2011 through 2024, securing eight race victories during his time in the sport. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has concluded his Formula One racing career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: The Spanish driver competing for Williams has secured four Grand Prix victories during his 12-year Formula One career.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class. He competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to sports car racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently functioning as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing full-time in Formula One throughout 2021-2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One. He has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024, along with 73 Grand Prix victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have raced in Formula One, competing in the championship between 2022 and 2024. He currently fulfills a reserve driver role for the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from their Enstone base since 2021, this Formula One team was rebranded to promote Renault's Alpine sports car marque after competing as the manufacturer's works squad under the Renault name. The team maintained its factory status throughout Renault's involvement in the sport, which concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has entered Formula One competition through multiple organizational structures, with its current racing operation competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and stands as the sport's most storied competitor, participating continuously in Formula One since its inaugural 1950 season. The team, colloquially known as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains both the longest-running and most decorated outfit in the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the sport in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970, initially achieved success in endurance racing before transitioning to Formula One in 1993. Over three decades as an independent constructor, the team competed in the sport while undergoing various transformations, ultimately ceasing operations in 2025 as one of motorsport's longest-tenured grid participants. Audi acquired the organization and its infrastructure in 2024 to establish its own Formula One presence.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technological facility in Woking. Currently operating under a Mastercard partnership agreement, the team functions as part of the broader McLaren Group structure and is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current incarnation based in Brackley operating under a German licence. The team, now jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal shares since 2022, competes as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team and carries on the storied "Silver Arrows" legacy.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as the second racing entity under Red Bull's ownership. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Red Bull GmbH racing portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that joined the grid in 2024, operating as a sister squad to Red Bull Racing under the Red Bull GmbH umbrella. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its partner team in Milton Keynes, it represents one of two constructor operations within Red Bull's Formula One portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team established in 2005 and based in England, operating as one of two teams within the Red Bull GmbH motorsport portfolio. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the principal role thereafter. The team competes alongside Racing Bulls, the conglomerate's second Formula One entry.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
